descriptions.sales_transactions: One row per sale: one product bought by one customer at one franchise at one time. There is no separate orders table. Synthetic data from 2023-01-01 to 2025-12-30, millions of rows: filter by dateTime or aggregate, do not select everything.
descriptions.sales_transactions.franchiseID: The franchise (shop) that made the sale. Joins to sales_franchises.franchiseID.
descriptions.sales_transactions.dateTime: When the sale happened (timestamp). Use year(dateTime), month(dateTime) for year and month questions.
descriptions.sales_transactions.product: Name of the cookie sold. Exactly six values: Austin Almond Biscotti, Outback Oatmeal, Tokyo Tidbits, Orchard Oasis, Pearly Pies, Golden Gate Ginger.
descriptions.sales_transactions.unitPrice: Price of one unit. It is 3 for every product.
descriptions.sales_transactions.totalPrice: quantity * unitPrice: the revenue of this sale. Revenue is SUM(totalPrice).
descriptions.sales_transactions.paymentMethod: Card network, lowercase: visa, mastercard or amex.
descriptions.sales_transactions.cardNumber: The customer's card number. Sensitive: never select it unless the question asks for it. Use paymentMethod for payment questions.
descriptions.sales_customers: One row per customer (300). Customers live in Australia, the USA and Japan.
descriptions.sales_customers.customerID: Unique id of the customer. Joins to sales_transactions.customerID.
descriptions.sales_customers.email_address: Sensitive. Do not select unless asked.
descriptions.sales_customers.phone_number: Sensitive. Do not select unless asked.
descriptions.sales_customers.address: Sensitive street address. Do not select unless asked.
descriptions.sales_customers.country: Country name as written for customers: Australia, USA or Japan. Franchises write the United States as 'US', customers write 'USA'.
descriptions.sales_customers.continent: Customer continent, for example Asia or Oceania.
descriptions.sales_customers.postal_zip_code: Postal or zip code as a number.
descriptions.sales_franchises: One row per franchise shop (48). Each franchise sells the cookies and is tied to one supplier.
descriptions.sales_franchises.franchiseID: Unique id of the franchise. Joins to sales_transactions.franchiseID and media_customer_reviews.franchiseID.
descriptions.sales_franchises.name: Name of the shop, for example Tokyo Treats. Use it when a question asks which franchise.
descriptions.sales_franchises.district: District or neighbourhood of the shop.
descriptions.sales_franchises.country: Country of the shop: Japan, US, Australia, Canada, Netherlands, France, Germany, Italy or Sweden. The United States is 'US' here, not 'USA'.
descriptions.sales_franchises.size: Shop size class as text: S, M, L, XL or XXL.
descriptions.sales_franchises.supplierID: The franchise's supplier. Joins to sales_suppliers.supplierID. Only 27 suppliers exist for 48 franchises, so a join to sales_suppliers keeps only the 27 franchises whose supplier is listed.
descriptions.sales_suppliers.supplierID: Unique id of the supplier. Joins to sales_franchises.supplierID.
descriptions.sales_suppliers.name: Supplier name.
descriptions.sales_suppliers.ingredient: The ingredient supplied: cacao, coconut, almonds, cane sugar, vanilla, pecans, hazelnuts, cinnamon, cashews, maple syrup, pistachios or oats.
descriptions.sales_suppliers.continent: Supplier continent: Asia, Europe, North America, Central America or South America.
descriptions.sales_suppliers.size: Supplier size class as text: S, M, L, XL or XXL.
descriptions.sales_suppliers.approved: 'Y' when the supplier is approved. Every supplier is currently 'Y'.
descriptions.media_customer_reviews: One row per written customer review of a franchise: free text in review. Use this table for questions about reviews. Joins to sales_franchises on franchiseID.
descriptions.media_customer_reviews.review: The review text, long free text.
descriptions.media_gold_reviews_chunked: The reviews cut into chunks for search: one row per chunk of text, so counting rows here does not count reviews. Use media_customer_reviews for review questions.

expressions.best-selling product: the product with the highest SUM(quantity) in sales_transactions (rank by revenue only if the question says so)
expressions.average sale value: AVG(totalPrice) over sales_transactions, since each row is one sale

examples.question: How many suppliers are there on each continent?
examples.sql: SELECT continent, count(*) FROM sales_suppliers GROUP BY continent

examples.question: How many franchises are there in each country?
examples.sql: SELECT country, count(*) FROM sales_franchises GROUP BY country

examples.question: What is the number of units sold per payment method?
examples.sql: SELECT paymentMethod, sum(quantity) FROM sales_transactions GROUP BY paymentMethod

instructions: Use Databricks SQL, for example year(dateTime), month(dateTime) and date_trunc. Tables are in the connected schema: use bare table names such as sales_transactions.
Join sales_transactions to sales_franchises on franchiseID and to sales_customers on customerID. Join sales_franchises to sales_suppliers on supplierID.
Revenue is SUM(totalPrice). Each row of sales_transactions is one sale of one product, so count rows for the number of sales.
Country spellings differ between tables: customers use 'USA', franchises use 'US'. Match the spelling of the table you filter on.
Never select cardNumber, email_address, phone_number or address unless the question asks for them.
sales_transactions has millions of rows: aggregate it or filter it by dateTime, and never run SELECT * on it.
